question: The Archaea differ from the bacteria in that:

options.opa: Their membranes have a single phospholipid layer.
options.opd: They are not susceptible to viral infection.
options.ope: They do not have a cell wall.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Archaea -> differ from bacteria -> in having membranes with glycerol ethers -> 80% CHAIN: Archaea -> have unique membrane composition -> glycerol ethers instead of phospholipid layer -> 85% CHAIN: Archaea -> exhibit resistance to viral infection -> 70% CHAIN: Archaea -> lack a cell wall -> 80%
enhanced_information: Archaea differ from bacteria in that their membranes have glycerol ethers, not a single phospholipid layer. This is supported by the unique membrane composition of Archaea. Additionally, Archaea are not susceptible to viral infection and lack a cell wall.
analysis: Archaea differ from bacteria primarily in their membrane composition, having glycerol ethers instead of a single phospholipid layer. They are also not susceptible to viral infection and lack a cell wall. These characteristics align with known facts about Archaea.
